disagreements: Decision 1's verbatim signature `pub fn check<P, C>(shell: &Shell<P, C>)` does not type-check here: `Shell` is declared as `Shell<P, C, S>` (lib.rs:169) with three type parameters and no default, so `&Shell<P, C>` (two args) is not a valid Rust type. Implemented as `pub fn check<P, C, S>(shell: &Shell<P, C, S>) -> Outcome<()>`; behavior is identical.

Decision 1's verbatim import `use crate::shell::{Shell, ShellCondition};` cannot resolve: `crate::shell` does not contain `Shell` (the struct is defined at the crate root, `crate::Shell`, lib.rs:169); only `ShellCondition` lives in `crate::shell` (shell.rs:975). Split into `use crate::Shell;` and `use crate::shell::ShellCondition;`.

Decision 4's test-module header `use truck_topology::*;` cannot resolve from inside the truck-topology crate itself (there is no `extern crate self as truck_topology`); the in-crate `#[cfg(test)]` module uses `use crate::*;` instead. Doctests are external crates, so the full path works there as written.

Decision 4's instruction to copy the `ShellCondition` doc witnesses verbatim into in-crate tests is not compilable as-is because in-crate test code is subject to crate lints that doctest code is not: `Vertex::news(&[(); N])` trips `clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args` (denied by `#![deny(clippy::all)]`, lib.rs:72) so the needless borrow was dropped to `Vertex::news([(); N])`, and the witnesses' `v[i]`/`edge[i]`/`shell[5]` indexing trips the `clippy::indexing_slicing` deny inherited from `invariants/mod.rs`, so the test module carries `#[allow(clippy::indexing_slicing)]` with an H-1 justification comment. The constructed shells are identical to the doc examples.
